flags: minor: overlaps conceptually with R041-09 and R041-10 (individual-vs-group distinction), though each tests a different skill
R041-01.notes: C covers the whole arc: flawed story, lab finding about individuals, Philpot group finding, reconciliation. A distorts (city vs small town, 'proved'); B contradicts P5 ('do not necessarily contradict'); D 'now agree' is unsupported and omits the field findings.

R041-02.notes: P1 describes the Genovese story and says it inspired research. C is P2 content, D is P4 content, B is unsupported argument.

R041-03.notes: Paraphrase of 'assuming that someone else will act.' A, B, C are not mentioned.

R041-04.notes: Second explanation is social cues: if no one seems alarmed, the situation may not seem like an emergency. D is the well-built trap drawn from the first explanation (diffusion of responsibility); the stem's 'second explanation' rules it out cleanly.

R041-05.notes: 'staged emergencies' = arranged/set up. C is the tempting literal theater sense.

R041-06.notes: P3 notes the effect was reproduced, then pivots to the Genovese story's inaccuracies. A contradicts 'reproduced'; B is P4; C is only the first clause, not the main role.

flags: minor: very easy verbatim lookup ('nine of every ten'); acceptable as a detail item but adds little discrimination
R041-07.notes: Direct detail from P4. Fact check: Philpot et al. 2019 (American Psychologist) found intervention in about 91% of 219 conflicts in the UK, the Netherlands, and South Africa, so the passage is accurate.

R041-08.notes: Real security-camera footage vs staged emergencies. A describes Darley/Latane; C contradicts P4; D is unsupported.

R041-09.notes: Last paragraph: individuals in crowds help less, yet a crowd as a whole is more likely to produce a helper. Only D has both parts. B is the 'classic indifference' reading the author rejects; A reverses the individual-level effect; C denies both.

flags: minor: key is the longest choice and the only nuanced, mixed-attitude option, a mild cue typical of attitude items
R041-10.notes: The author accepts the individual-level finding ('a person in a crowd may indeed be less likely to act') but reframes its lesson as being about divided responsibility, not indifference. B: the author does not dismiss it. C: the author is critical. D: the author explicitly reconciles the findings.
